problem_motivation.content: Fusion materials must withstand extreme radiation, temperature, and stress.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: One remaining challenge is that of materials, which can withstand extreme conditions of radiation, temperature, and stress, with long-term steady properties for the power plant to be economically viable

prior_limitation.content: The quaternary alloy formed embrittling Cr- and V-rich precipitates.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, this quaternary RHEA demonstrated Cr- and V-rich precipitates which could be detrimental to mechanical properties in terms of embrittlement.

rejected_alternative.content: Iron additions were rejected after producing unwanted intermetallic phases.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: the addition of Fe in both low and high elemental concentrations promotes the formation of several undesired intermetallic phases instead of single-phase solid-solution, as well as lowering the melting point of the system. Due to failure of this approach, a quinary HEA was planned

mechanism_principle.content: Irradiation hardening combines implantation, ballistic-mixing distortion, and grain refinement.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the increase after irradiation is a synergistic combination between Ar implantation, lattice distortion caused by irradiation ballistic mixing, and grain refinement.

hypothesis_statement.content: A quinary design should improve high-temperature and irradiation resistance.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In this study, a design strategy to further improve the overall response of the W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA is introduced and resulted in the development of a quinary RHEA with improved resistance to high-temperature and irradiation environments.

evidence_result.content: No dislocation loops appeared after severe dual-beam irradiation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Dislocation loops were not detected even after 8.5 dpa and at 9.13% He implantation during the dual-beam experiment

evidence_result.content: Hardness rose from 13.25 to 20 GPa through annealing and irradiation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The average hardness of the unirradiated sample was measured to be 13.25 GPa. After annealing the sample hardness increased to 16.25 GPa, while after irradiation the sample hardness reached a value of 20 GPa.

constraint.content: VEC must remain below 4.4 for stable BCC RHEAs.
constraint.evidence_span: It has been shown that BCC RHEAs can exhibit high-stability and suitable mechanical properties when the VEC value remains below 4.4

contradiction.content: Unlike the quaternary alloy, the quinary alloy did not precipitate under irradiation.
contradiction.evidence_span: This is unlike the W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA where irradiation led to uniform and dense Cr-V precipitation
